findings.description: R10 fires through intervening adjectives, and the relaxation keys on nothing enumerable: it asks only the strict version's own question (does this word end in "s") of up to four words after the count, with no adjective list, no suffix gate, and no part-of-speech guess.
findings.evidence: check-build.sh 'probe.py r10-adjective' exit 0, incl. "note this run's invented modifiers: nymmvgf, ercgmpp, pzjeqnxr" / "ok fires through 'nymmvgf'" ... "ok a correct count with adjectives stays silent". Code re-read at check-job-spec.py:1786-1802 — `_MODIFIER_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*")`, `_MAX_GOVERNING_WORDS = 4`, loop body `if word.endswith("s"): return True`. Independent end-to-end fixture I built (scratchpad/both3, spec excerpt "Four further rules constrain how the thing works:" over 3 bullets) -> "job-spec: [heuristic] R10 count-vs-list: tasks/T-001.md:24 says 'Four' (4) but the following list has 3 item(s)", exit 4. Direct call with six nonce modifiers generated in my own session (kscc, tgkqsvyk, sbnoqr, ctrc, shmvsyny, bujouj) -> all True; no allowlist written beforehand could contain them.

findings.description: Observation, not a violation of any cited clause: the four-word window widens R10's firing surface past adjectives to any filler word, so `2 or more artifacts:` above a three-item list now governs a plural noun where the strict predicate was silent — a shape C-2's archive sweep does not happen to contain.
findings.evidence: Direct call to `_governs_plural_noun`: "'2 or more artifacts:' -> True" (strict predicate returned False, since 'or' does not end in s). The bound errs safe in the other direction — 'Four further key new extra rules constrain how:' -> False, and "Four of the archive's shipped rules constrain how:" -> False, both silent rather than wrong. R10 is HEURISTIC in RULE_CLASS (check-job-spec.py:1067-1073), so any misfire exits 4 and prints the `**Lint exception**: R10` waiver path, as my fixture run showed. C-2's corpus sweep is green across all 11 archives, which is the false-positive evidence the constitution chose.

findings.description: R21 refuses a checker-deterministic task citing a judgment clause, reads the clause kind off the constitution rather than the task's check_method paraphrase, names only the offending clause, carries an explicit PROOF entry, and runs ahead of every heuristic in run_rules.
findings.evidence: check-build.sh 'probe.py r21-unsafe' exit 0 (16 assertions, incl. "message does NOT name the innocent clause C-1", "R21 carries an explicit PROOF entry in RULE_CLASS", "placement/R2: R21 is reported ahead of it", "placement/R10: ... at the unwaivable proof exit"). Re-derived independently rather than taken from the probe: (a) source — I built a fixture (scratchpad/inv) whose check_method paraphrase INVERTS the constitution, claiming C-1 is the rubric and C-2 the script while the constitution says the reverse; the linter reported "R21 checker-routing: tasks/T-001.md declares checker: checker-deterministic but cites C-2" at exit 1, naming the constitution's rubric clause and not the paraphrase's. Code at check-job-spec.py:1114-1133 reads `ctx.clauses.get(cid)` then `classify_check_text(clause.check_text)` and never touches `task.check_method_map`; `ctx.clauses` comes from `parse_constitution(const_text)` at :2073. (b) class — check-job-spec.py:573 `"R20": PROOF, "R21": PROOF,`. (c) placement — check-job-spec.py:2109 puts `lambda: rule_R21(ctx, audit_id)` third in `steps`, ahead of R2 (:2122), R9, R10, R12; my scratchpad/both3 fixture carrying BOTH defects reported the R21 proof at exit 1, while the same tree with only the heuristic reported "[heuristic] R10 count-vs-list" at exit 4. (d) CON-audit skip — check-job-spec.py:1115-1116 `if audit_id == "CON-audit": return None`; the same fixture that exits 1 under DEC-audit exits 0 under `--audit-id CON-audit`.

findings.description: Both legal routings stay silent: a checker-judgment task citing a rubric plus script clauses, and a checker-deterministic task whose only clauses are script-checked but whose check command contains the literal string checker-judgment: as an argument.
findings.evidence: check-build.sh 'probe.py r21-safe' exit 0: "ok neither legal shape trips R21" / "ok both legal shapes exit 0". Re-derived on fixtures I built: flipping scratchpad/inv's task to `checker: checker-judgment` (rubric clause still cited) -> "OK: ... passes check-job-spec (DEC-audit)", exit 0. scratchpad/lit, a `checker: checker-deterministic` task citing two script clauses where C-2's check is `.agent-guild/scripts/check-build.sh 'grep -q "checker-judgment:" notes.txt'` -> exit 0. R21's loop keys on `classify_check_text(...) == "judgment"`, which requires the check text to START with `checker-judgment:` (check-job-spec.py:1078-1085), not merely contain it.

findings.description: The R2 diagnostic quotes the matched anchor and states where it sits in the citing document; both positions read correctly, and the silence case stays silent.
findings.evidence: `probe.py r2-anchor` exit 0, so the mechanical half is settled. Ruling on the printed blocks: [A] "...quoting 'if val[0] == val[-1] and val[0] in (\'\"\', "\'"):', which sits at tasks/T-001.md:24 in the citing document—but that code is actually at src/fixture.py:29" — the anchor is quoted and a reader learns it sits at line 24 without opening the file; the probe's own header confirms 24 is where it sits. [B] "...which sits on this same line (tasks/T-001.md:22) in the citing document..." — the anchor shares the citation's line and the sentence says exactly that, naming the line too. [C] prints "(nothing emitted)", as required. The selection algorithm is untouched: `nearest_anchor`'s sentence bounds, exclusion, and distance comparison are byte-identical in the diff; only the return widened to `(start, content)`. The absence guard is intact — check_citation_rules still `continue`s when the span is absent from the whole target file.

findings.description: Scope and seam, checked as the task directs rather than as a full C-9 ruling (C-9 is not cited by T-001 and its suite cases belong to T-002): the required r2_anchor_message seam exists with a parameter named anchor, both consumer suites are green, only the owned file is modified, and nothing is committed.
findings.evidence: `inspect.signature(r2_anchor_message)` -> `(anchor, label, src_line, path, lineno, actual_line, anchor_line)`; name and first parameter both match, and the parameter is POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD so a wrapper can bind it by name — I called `f(anchor="X-ANCHOR", ...)` and got both the "sits at t/T.md:24" and "sits on this same line (t/T.md:22)" forms. Defined at check-job-spec.py:937. `--self-test` -> "OK: self-test passed (12 fixtures)", exit 0; `test_check_job_spec.py` -> "230 passed, 0 failed", exit 0 — re-run after the tree changed under me, still green. A later read added " M .agent-guild/scripts/test_check_job_spec.py"; that is NOT T-001's, it is T-002 landing on the path it declares in `owns` (tasks/T-002.md:27, status needs-check) while I was checking — mtimes are test_check_job_spec.py 2026-08-19T00:27:06 against check-job-spec.py 2026-08-19T00:20:41, so T-001's artifact has not moved since I ran the probes. `git log --oneline -1` -> ae3f757, the pre-job commit, so nothing was committed and C-7's working-tree read stays non-empty.
